# Sitecast

Record any website as an MP4 video directly on your local machine.

*An example of a video generated by Sitecast:*

<div align="center">
  <video src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2ae1f83-b0e8-4713-87e1-09d3c83ab635" width="100%" controls autoplay></video>
</div>

Sitecast opens a webpage in a real headed Chromium instance, scrolls through it naturally at a human-like pace, and records the output as a high-quality MP4 video using FFmpeg.

## Why Sitecast?

- **100% Local**: No cloud accounts, no API keys, and no subscriptions. Everything runs on your own hardware.
- **Privacy-focused**: Your data never leaves your machine. Perfect for recording internal dashboards or sensitive content.
- **High Quality**: Captures crisp video using `libx264` (CRF 23) out of the box, ensuring near-lossless quality for screen content.
- **Natural Scrolling**: Automatically scrolls top-to-bottom in a way that looks human, capturing all scroll-triggered animations.

## Features

- Custom viewport dimensions and framerates (up to 60fps)
- Dark mode support (`prefers-color-scheme: dark`)
- Kiosk mode (hide the browser chrome/UI)
- Built-in environment diagnostics (`sitecast doctor`)
- Fallback Chromium installation via Playwright (`sitecast setup`)

## Installation

Sitecast requires Linux, Node.js 18+, FFmpeg, and Xvfb.

```bash
# Install the CLI globally
npm install -g sitecast

# Check if your system is ready
sitecast doctor
```

If you are missing system dependencies, see the [CLI Documentation](./packages/cli/README.md#setup) for detailed setup instructions.

## Quick Start

Record a website with default settings (720p, 30fps):

```bash
sitecast render https://example.com
```

The video will be saved as `sitecast-<timestamp>.mp4` in your current directory.

Record in 1080p, 60fps, dark mode, without the browser frame:

```bash
sitecast render https://example.com --width 1920 --height 1080 --fps 60 --dark-mode --no-browser-frame
```
